title: Traditional-character field population policy
author: author-b
description: Day 1 records a project-specific policy for a Chinese-card field: it is never auto-converted, instead receiving a specific literal placeholder token. Day 6 must recall that exact placeholder token. Auto-converting simplified-to-traditional text is the obvious default a general-knowledge model would assume, so a memory-less model has no way to guess this project deliberately rejects that and uses this specific placeholder string instead.
day1_prompt: We're deciding how the `TraditionalChars` field is populated on each card in our Chinese-vocab pipeline. Decide and record: this field is NEVER auto-converted from the simplified text — instead, the pipeline writes the literal placeholder value `PENDING_MANUAL` into it, so a human fills it in by hand later.
memory_sentence: The `TraditionalChars` field is never auto-converted from simplified text; the pipeline writes the literal placeholder value `PENDING_MANUAL` into it so a human fills it in by hand later.
canon_heading: TraditionalChars field uses a manual placeholder, never auto-conversion
day_n_prompt: It's day 6. When a new card is created, what literal placeholder value gets written into the `TraditionalChars` field instead of an auto-converted value? Answer with only the placeholder value.

swap.day1_prompt: We're deciding how the `TraditionalChars` field is populated on each card in our Chinese-vocab pipeline. Decide and record: this field IS auto-converted from the simplified text at card-creation time, using a small conversion library we're calling `hanzi-convert`, with no manual step.
swap.memory_sentence: The `TraditionalChars` field is auto-converted from simplified text at card-creation time using the `hanzi-convert` library, with no manual step.
swap.canon_heading: TraditionalChars field is auto-converted via hanzi-convert
